questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic opportunities. I had some lecturers who recommended the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. The International Programmes Administrator sent a lot of information, which helped a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an online induction.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. The university have a partnership with Manchester Student Accomodation, through which I found a room in an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It may be harder to find friends, but I really enjoyed having my own space where I could relax. The apartment wasn't very tidy, but it may not be a general problem.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As i remember it, most of the registration happened through the ERASMUS-portal. The only time I had to be there physically was when I had to get my student-ID-card issued.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Programmes Administrator was always helpful in case I needed any information or wanted to change the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only ended up having one of my three chosen courses. Changing the courses was no problem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You may not get the courses you want, so don't get to exited about specific courses. I ended up having two courses that I didn't initially choose, but ended up becoming my favorite courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The general level was pretty high - the lecturers were very competent and had expectations to us.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was way more interactive, and the lecturers took us (the students) more seriously, wanted to learn our names, chatted with us in the breaks etc. Overall it felt like they had an ambition to bridge the gap between students and lecturers that something can occur.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Screening Culture, Anthropology of Displacement and Migration and Anthropology of Vision, Senses and Memory.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anthropology of Vision, Senses and Memory is one of a kind. A good general introduction to phenomenology in anthropology and beyond. There were some nice multi-modal exercises, and the lecturer, Andrew Irving is one of a kind. I highly recommend it.

questions.answer: Bus tickets are expensive in Manchester - ride a bike!

questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, book clubs etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Drinking beers at a pub is always a good way to get to know people in the UK. A part from that use the facilities in the Student Union, talk to the other students in the pauses or start playing something.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Lake District. The Peak District. Liverpool. Edinburgh. Northern Wales. League 2-football.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was alright.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in the breaks and check out the societies on the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The students are generally younger, so I felt pretty old compared to a lot of my co-students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You will get friends at some point, use the breaks to get to know your co-student and don't isolate yourself if you don't have anyone to talk to within the first weeks.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I improved my language skills and had to learn to navigate in a new country with other systems.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of reading material.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
